statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON (green). Tail risk is low at 12% while stress is elevated at 54%, reflecting a fourth consecutive Nasdaq-100 lower close and a roughly 2.5% weekly decline set against an overnight futures session that has recovered inside a contained, two-sided band with the VIX decaying, oil easing and 2Y/10Y/30Y yields marginally lower.
recommendation: Tail remains well below the block threshold, so the deterministic mapping resolves to EA_ON for both NQ futures and the NAS100 CFD across the full 24-hour horizon. Conditional risk is concentrated in two structural checkpoints: the 13:30 UTC cash open together with the 13:45 UTC S&P Global flash PMI, published as the narrow 13:00-14:00 UTC danger window, and the 19:00-20:00 UTC power hour in which August monthly options expiration settles into the cash close ahead of the 21:00 UTC weekend halt. headline: Overnight recovery inside a contained two-sided band keeps Nasdaq-100 mean reversion intact after a fourth lower close, with the cash open, a flash PMI and monthly expiration as the day's checkpoints
body:
The Nasdaq-100 closed at 29,213.17 on 20 August, down 0.72% and roughly 2.5% on the week, a fourth consecutive lower close. The decline has been a grind rather than a rout: the session traded between 29,378.81 and 29,118.07 and closed about 95 points above its low, so retracements have remained available throughout the drawdown. Nine of the eleven S&P 500 sectors finished lower on the day. Overnight, NQ futures have recovered to roughly 29,407 against the 29,300.50 prior close, inside a two-sided band of about 29,274.25 to 29,464.25, and have already pulled back from the top of that band. That is a drift within a contained range rather than the shallow-pullback, repeated-extension structure that would threaten mean reversion, and no failed retracement has been observed.

The long end of the Treasury curve remains the driver of the weekly decline, but it is stable at the time of this assessment. The 10-year trades near 4.70%, the 2-year near 4.19% and the 30-year near 5.25%, each marginally lower on the day, after the 30-year reached its highest level in nearly two decades earlier in the week. Wednesday's Treasury announcement of larger long-end buybacks produced a rally that faded on Thursday, which is the immediate reason for the current stress level rather than for any tail reading. Volatility is decaying: the VIX is 15.81, down 1.25% from its 16.01 close, inside a session range of only 15.77 to 15.88, and delayed cross-asset context shows VIX futures easing and gold firmer on a softer dollar.

Energy remains the second macro overhang. WTI trades near $86.00, down 0.96% on the day but on course for a second consecutive weekly gain of roughly 6%, with Brent at $93.15 after touching a one-month high of $94.71 and then seeing profit-taking. The drivers are the US sanctions package directed at Iran and a Strait of Hormuz that remains closed. That is a persistent stress input rather than a new discontinuity, and today's easing marginally reduces the inflation impulse. In Europe, the STOXX 600 is little changed at 650.79, up 0.06%, and heading for a second straight weekly decline.

Delayed cross-asset context shows modestly constructive equity indications, with index futures higher by a few tenths of a percent and most tracked megacaps and semiconductors marginally positive, but the magnitudes are small and the section is labelled latest-session rather than live, so it is treated as confirmation of a benign backdrop rather than as evidence of directional structure. Today's scheduled structure is light: the S&P Global flash PMI at 13:45 UTC is the only meaningful US release, the Baker Hughes rig count follows at 17:00 UTC, and August monthly options expiration settles into the 20:00 UTC cash close before futures halt at 21:00 UTC for the weekend. Next week carries the heavier stack, with the GDP second estimate and Core PCE together on 26 August, a major semiconductor earnings call the same evening, and the Jackson Hole symposium running 27-29 August, for which the organiser has not published a keynote time and which is therefore excluded from the event array rather than timestamped by guess.

outlookSummary: The horizon runs from the current European mid-morning through a full European and US session and then ends inside the weekend futures halt. Early European hours are scored at low tail risk on the contained, two-sided overnight band. Conditional risk rises into the US pre-market and peaks in the 13:00-14:00 UTC hour, which contains both the 13:30 UTC cash open and the 13:45 UTC S&P Global flash PMI and is published as the narrow danger window. A second, slightly lower peak falls on the 19:00-20:00 UTC power hour, where August monthly options expiration settles into the cash close alongside weekend risk reduction. Every hour of the horizon maps to EA_ON, because no published tail score reaches the block threshold. From the 21:00 UTC CME halt onward the scores are held flat and low: no continuous price path exists over the weekend, so accumulating headline risk is carried as gap risk at the Sunday reopen, which falls outside this horizon, and confidence steps down gradually to reflect the ageing of the last live observation rather than any deterioration in the evidence itself.
